results.description:
Forfeit is an app that adds accountability to your habits. We're based on the scientifically backed concept of Habit Contracts - popularised by Atomic Habits - that adding accountability to completing habits is massively effective.

Our 20k+ users have achieved a 94% success rate on over 75k forfeits.

HOW IT WORKS
1. Set your forfeit
Set the task/habit that you want to complete, when you want to complete it by, and how you'll be held accountable if you don't complete it. This can be sending an accountability buddy a text or email!

2. Submit your evidence
Verify that you completed your habit using any of the methods defined below. This can be in the form of a photo, timelapse, self-verify, friend verify, GPS check-in, a web tracking limit, an Apple Health activity, a Strava run, a Whoop activity, a MyFitnessPal meal or anything else.

3. Or you fail
If you don't send evidence in time, your accountability method is triggered. This rarely happens - only 6% of forfeits fail. If you do fail, you can appeal the failed forfeit - we only want you to fail if it's a willpower issue, not if life gets in the way!


VERIFICATION METHODS
• Photo
Take a photo of the task that you completed, and an AI will verify if your photo matches your description.
Examples: At the gym, inbox zero, Duolingo completed, homework submitted, taking medication.

• Timelapse
Record a timelapse of you completing the tasks that you completed, and a human will verify if your timelapse matches your description.
Examples: Meditating, nighttime routine, stretching, working for 1hr.

• Self-Verify
Simply verify if you completed this task. No need for evidence!
Examples: No smoking, no drinking, no vaping, absolutely anything!

• Friend-Verify
Have an accountability buddy testify to whether you did or didn't complete a task.
Examples: No drinking, no phone in the house, no eating junk food.

• Apple Health
Set a threshold that you must cross in Apple Health (eg, 10,000 steps). Thousands of apps sync to this.
Examples: 10,000 steps, 20 mins meditation, 30 min bike ride, less than 2000 calories consumed.

• GPS Check-in
Set a GPS location that you must be within 100m of by the deadline.
Examples: Check into the gym, work on time, home by a certain time.

• Location Reminders
Get a reminder when you arrive at or leave a place you've saved, even when Forfeit is closed. Background location is optional.
Examples: "You're home - time to walk the dog", "At the gym - log your workout".

• GPS Avoid
Set a location that you won't be within a certain radius of at the deadline.
Examples: Not being at a bar on the weekends, leaving the house at a certain time.

• RescueTime integration
We sync with RescueTime, a web time-tracking app. You can use this to set thresholds on websites/desktop apps.
Examples: Max 30 mins on reddit.com, minimum 2hrs on VSCode, max 30 mins on gmail.com

• Pomodoro timer
This is a timer that if you click off, you fail.
Examples: Working for 30 mins, meditating for 20 mins, studying for 45 mins.



OTHER FEATURES
• X days/week: Set forfeits to be due a certain number of times per week (eg, work out 3x/week)
• Certain days/week: Set forfeits only to be due on certain days (eg, weekdays, or Mo/We/Fr)
• Appeal anything: If you have to skip a submission, simply send in an appeal, and it'll be reviewed in a few hours by a human.
• Varying leniency modes: Depending on your leniency mode (lenient, normal, hard), you may or may not be required to justify your appeal with evidence. Hard mode doesn't allow appeals.
• Screen Time integration: If you go over your limit, you're held accountable.

Twice A Day is a personal accountability system for people who already know what to do—but struggle to consistently follow through.

Most productivity apps help you make plans. Twice A Day helps you keep them.

HOW IT WORKS

1. Decide what matters

Choose a few realistic priorities for your day. Add them manually, talk through them with your voice, or get intelligent suggestions from your calendar, mail and notes.

2. Lock in your commitments

When you’re ready, commit to your plan. Once it’s locked, tasks can’t be changed, deleted or pushed to tomorrow.

Because if you can rewrite the plan whenever things get difficult, it isn’t really a commitment.

3. Follow through

Twice A Day remembers what you said you would do and brings you back to it throughout the day. Your commitments stay visible, even after the motivation that created them fades.

4. Reflect honestly

Come back at the end of your day and close the loop. Review what you completed, acknowledge what you didn’t and understand what got in the way.

ACCOUNTABILITY THAT GETS MORE PERSONAL

Over time, Twice A Day helps you see:

• Where you consistently follow through
• Where you avoid or procrastinate
• When you’re taking on too much
• Which priorities keep getting neglected
• How your actions align with your goals
• Whether you’re becoming more consistent

Your weekly reports turn your actual behavior into personalized insights, helping you make better commitments and recognize the patterns holding you back.

WHEN YOU NEED MORE SUPPORT

• Brain-dump tasks using your voice
• Get smart suggestions from the tools you already use
• Ask your AI coach for motivation or guidance
• Track promises kept, perfect days and your Self-Trust Score
• Connect daily commitments to your long-term goals

Twice A Day isn’t about doing as much as possible.

It’s about deciding what matters, making a realistic promise to yourself and keeping it.

Twice-a-day check-ins. All-day accountability.

Plan. Commit. Follow through. Reflect.

An Audit Punch List is an essential tool in project management and quality assurance, designed to ensure that all aspects of a project meet the required standards and specifications before final completion. Whether you’re managing a construction project, conducting a financial audit, or overseeing a compliance review, an effective audit punch list helps identify and address any outstanding issues, ensuring that nothing is overlooked.

What is an Audit Punch List?
An audit punch list is a detailed checklist used during the final stages of a project to verify that all tasks have been completed satisfactorily. It typically includes a comprehensive list of items that need to be inspected, reviewed, or corrected. This list is crucial for maintaining quality control, ensuring compliance with industry standards, and achieving project objectives within the stipulated timeframe and budget.
To develop a comprehensive audit punch list, follow these steps:

Define Objectives: Clearly outline the goals of the audit to ensure the punch list aligns with project requirements.
Identify Key Areas: Determine the critical components that need inspection, such as safety measures, compliance standards, and project specifications.
Detail Specific Tasks: Break down each key area into actionable items, specifying what needs to be checked, who is responsible, and the expected completion date.
Use Technology: Utilize project management software to create, manage, and track the punch list efficiently. Tools like Asana, Trello, or specialized audit software can enhance organization and collaboration.
Regular Reviews: Schedule periodic reviews of the punch list to monitor progress, address new issues, and ensure timely completion of all tasks.
Benefits of Using an Audit Punch List
Implementing an audit punch list in your project management process offers several advantages:

Increased Efficiency: Streamlines the final inspection process, making it easier to manage and complete tasks systematically.
Higher Compliance: Ensures that all regulatory and contractual obligations are met, reducing the risk of non-compliance penalties.
Better Documentation: Provides a clear record of completed and pending tasks, which is invaluable for future audits and project evaluations.
Customer Satisfaction: Delivering a thoroughly vetted project enhances client trust and satisfaction, leading to repeat business and positive referrals.
Conclusion
An audit punch list is a vital component of successful project management, ensuring that every detail is accounted for and that the project meets all quality and compliance standards. By meticulously planning, executing, and reviewing your audit punch list, you can achieve higher efficiency, mitigate risks, and deliver outstanding results. Incorporate an audit punch list into your workflow today to enhance your project outcomes and maintain excellence in every endeavor.

Oathly is a social habit tracker built on accountability with friends. Make a pact: what you'll do, how often, and the stakes if you miss. Prove it with a photo, keep your streak, and let the forfeit count when you don't.

Check in with a photo taken in the app. Your friend confirms it, or calls you out. Miss, and the forfeit you agreed goes on a shared ledger you can both see. It's accountability with friends in the plainest sense: someone else knows whether you did the thing.

HOW IT WORKS
• Make a pact: daily, a few times a week, or a one off with a deadline
• Send your friend a link. They open it, sign in, and join
• Check in with a photo, or an honour tap if that's what you agreed
• Your partner approves it or rejects it
• Build a streak. Miss, and the forfeit is recorded against you
• Settle up in real life, then you both mark it done

OATHLY NEVER TOUCHES MONEY
The forfeit is between you and your friend. Oathly writes it down and keeps score. It does not take payments, hold funds, move money or process a transfer, and it never will. The ledger is bookkeeping between two people and nothing more. What you owe each other, and whether you pay it, is entirely up to you.

WHY ACCOUNTABILITY WITH FRIENDS WORKS
A habit tracker you only answer to yourself is easy to quietly let slide. A social habit tracker with someone checking isn't. Streaks and stakes both help, but the thing that actually changes behaviour is knowing a specific person will see, this week, whether you did what you said you'd do.

YOUR PROOF STAYS BETWEEN YOU
Proof photos are visible only to the members of that pact. There is no public feed, no discovery, no browsing strangers. Location data written into a photo by your camera is stripped on your phone before the photo is uploaded, so a check in from home does not tell anyone where you live.

WHAT PEOPLE MAKE PACTS ABOUT
The gym, three mornings a week, with a photo from the parking lot. A daily language lesson before either of you checks your phone. No smoking, checked in every evening with an honour tap. A shared project with a deadline neither of you wants to be the one who missed. The app encourages users to record their interactions with police officers and upload them to a publicly accessible database. The goal is to create a transparent record of police interactions with the public and increase accountability, as well as highlight good police behavior.

WatchR also includes a feature for users to rate their interactions with individual police officers. This helps other users know which officers have a track record of treating people fairly and professionally, and which ones may have a history of misconduct. Additionally, WatchR provides resources for users to learn more about their legal rights when interacting with the police.

The public database created by WatchR is accessible to anyone, including journalists, researchers, and community activists. By making this data available to the public, users can help shed light on any patterns of misconduct or abuse of power by individual police officers. This information can be used to hold officers accountable for their actions and push for reforms to improve police accountability.

Overall, WatchR is a powerful tool for promoting police accountability and increasing transparency in police interactions with the public. By using WatchR to record and share their experiences, users can help drive meaningful change in the way law enforcement operates in their communities.

Soberphone is not just another app blocker. It's a real path out of screen addiction.

Social support is one of the most effective tools we have for breaking hard habits. It has decades of research behind it and is core to behavior change of all kinds. 

So we're putting it at the center of Soberphone because we want real solutions. We want freedom from our screens. We want to go beyond the blockers, gamification, and focus-hacks. 

Here's how it works:

1.) Decide what tech you struggle with and set goals for your ideal use. 

2.) Choose how long to use that tech for at each open with the "Unlock" Timer.

3.) Add supporters to motivate real change – they’ll be invited to check in if you go over a goal.

4.) Watch your orb – it changes to reflect your progress. Keep it vibrant by meeting your goals each day.


- THE CONTEXT -

There's a lot to love about our **screens**
The utility, the connection, the whole world in our hands.

But we're totally **hooked**
Hours, weeks, and years of our lives spent unintentionally absorbed.

We're not meant to face this **alone**
It takes a lot more than willpower to get free. And most existing solutions miss the emotional and relational core of the issue.

Healing happens in **connection** not in isolation.
Decades of research on compulsion and addiction are clear on this.

**Peer Support** is one of the most evidence-backed methods for breaking habits. So let's use it. 

No cold turkey.
No dumb phones.
No hyper-gamification.

Just flexible support for the screen-life balance you want.

you know what you should be doing. you're not doing it.

here's the fix: pick a rival. pick a habit. put real money on the line. check in with a photo. your rival decides if it counts.

Give your apps a gym rule.

Vaulted connects access to selected iPhone apps with a gym or another place you choose. It works alongside your own workout program, with no workout content or account setup.

START WITH FREE MANUAL

1. Save your gym or another meaningful place.
2. Choose apps, categories, or websites using Apple's private Screen Time picker.
3. Check your location and check in when your iPhone reports that it is inside your saved zone.
4. Use your selected apps during the visit. They relock when you end the visit or iOS detects that you have left.

Free Manual includes one saved place, one manual Vault, private app selection, manual check-ins, progress, and 30 days of history. This during-visit access does not earn Reward Passes for later.

TRY VAULTED AUTOMATIC

After purchase status is confirmed as Free, complete a manual visit of at least one minute to start your one-time 14-day Automatic preview. The preview requires no payment, never automatically charges, and does not renew or require cancellation.

Automatic adds a separate choice: bank up to 10 elapsed minutes per completed Vault session for later timed Reward Passes, with up to 300 minutes held in the Time Bank. It also includes optional arrival and exit automation, recurring schedule Vaults, more Vaults and places, full history, streak protection, and export.

Keep using Free Manual after the preview, or choose the optional one-time lifetime purchase. Automatic is a restorable non-consumable, with no subscription. The purchase screen shows your localized App Store price.

PERMISSIONS AND LOCATION

Vaulted explains location and Screen Time permissions during setup. Opening selected apps for a manual visit requires Allow Always location access so an on-device iOS safety region can relock them after a background exit. Automatic arrival and exit also use region monitoring.

GPS can drift indoors and iOS can delay region events. Vaulted provides status and recovery controls. It records device-reported location conditions and elapsed visits; it does not verify exercise, workout quality, or physical presence.

YOUR DATA

Apple's picker does not reveal selected app names to Vaulted. Apple-issued selection tokens are stored locally in the private App Group shared with its Screen Time extensions.

Saved places and visit history stay on your device and are not sent to Vaulted's servers. Vaulted does not continuously record your movement. Apple Maps handles map and search requests; purchases use Apple and RevenueCat.

Analytics and diagnostics are off by default and require opt-in. Delete My Data clears local app data and native Screen Time automation state. App Store purchase records remain available for Restore Purchases.

Overcoming addiction is hard. With Quitzilla you can follow all of your bad habits or addictions and use the app as help to analyze them and beat them. Stay clean and sober, overcome any addiction or habit which is holding you back from becoming a better version of yourself.

BAD HABITS TRACKER
Commit to quit "cold turkey"! You can add the exact day of the last time you did it, the money you usually spend on it, and let it serve as your starting point. From then on you can get tons of interesting statistics about it. The abstinence time and money saved are the leading statistics. 

REWARDS
The rewards feature is actually a calculation of the money saved. For example, if you’ve spent $100 on gambling weekly, and you haven’t gambled for a week, then those $100 are your weekly reward. This serves as great motivation to quit alcohol, cigarettes, junk food, or anything similar that costs us money and is bad for our body and health.

MOTIVATION
Quitzilla also features a motivation tab in which you can add your own reasons to quit your addiction and bad habits. Simply list all of the benefits of quitting and let them serve you as a motivation for you to continue your journey of overcoming addictions. 

USEFUL STATISTICS
The app keeps relevant statistics about each of your bad habits. From entering the day you quit and maximum abstinence period, to keep a record of the money, time spent on addiction, and average abstinence period.

QUOTE OF THE DAY
To keep you motivated and focused in your quest to get rid of the addictions, Quitzilla will display you “Quote of the Day” from various famous authors.

FEATURES:
- track multiple habits simultaneously.
- easy and simple tracking of bad habits and addictions
- help in quitting alcohol, drug, caffeine, food, sugar, etc.
- customize your bad habits
- rewards system
- motivation with reasons why to quit a certain habit
- detailed statistics about each addiction
- quote of the day for motivation and keeping focus
